questions.question: Which row operation is elementary?
options: Square every entry of a row.
Replace a row by the determinant of the matrix.
Replace one row by itself plus a multiple of another row.
questions.explanation: Adding a scalar multiple of one row to another is one of the three reversible elementary row operations.

questions.question: Why must the scalar be nonzero when multiplying a row in an elementary row operation?
options: Multiplication by zero would not be reversible.
Rows may never be multiplied by scalars.
questions.explanation: Scaling by $c\ne0$ is undone by scaling by $1/c$. At $c=0$, the original row is erased and no reciprocal exists.
